== Biography ==
=== Irish family roles, 24 October 2026 ===

Father [[Glasgow-1025|James]], specifically the James/Margaret Rutherford family-account role: [[Glasgow-1024|James]] 18%→78%, [[Glasgow-1492|Samuel]] 23%→76%, [[Glasgow-2425|Robert]] 18%→77%, [[Glasgow-2426|William]] 46%→84%, all now probable. The American [[Glasgow-12|Robert]]/[[Glasgow-649|Arthur]]/[[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] father grades remain35%, [[Glasgow-4027|John]] remains30%, [[Glasgow-4030|Mary]] remains22%; [[Glasgow-1025|James]]’s own [[Glasgow-1026|William]] father remains32%. The anonymous family recollection printed by Faris on p.9 explicitly gives James Glasgow, husband of Margaret Rutherford, four sons: William, Robert, James who settled near Moneymore, and Samuel who went to America, plus daughter Ellen. The letter-defined father is the family role represented by [[Glasgow-1025|James]]. These are specific named relationships, substantially stronger than the contributed-tree and locality summaries used by the earlier percentages. The same full-letter tradition was already read on 20 October; actual Faris pages now confirm its full structure. Its reproduction by Albert Rutherford and Faris’s pedigree are dependent presentations, not independent witnesses. The source links the named family roles; it does not identify this [[Glasgow-2872|Samuel]] with the testator or replace his existing John father. These are probable, not confident, relationships reconstructed from an anonymous retrospective family recollection, with no newly inspected parent register. The original letter remains uninspected. Faris calls the anonymous recollection file5 within PRONI T1959, while Rutherford’s reproduced copy cites T1959/3; retain this reference discrepancy pending archive checking. The 1759 probate index says Drumcarn and names no kin; neither that testator nor the inherited life dates are identified by this reassessment. The letter calls William eldest although the imported sibling birth estimates put him later; those estimates remain unverified. Faris also flags Samuel’s infant daughter and surviving mother-in-law in1824 against the supposed early paternal death. Those tensions require testing, not automatic exclusion. Preserve all existing people, vital fields, maternal grades and alternatives. No Scottish migration, identity merge, live edit or new father attachment is claimed.<ref>David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio(1990), printed pp.8–12; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-J pp.8–9], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13], DGS007834162, images1564–1566. PRONI T1959 anonymous family recollection, in [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ Albert Rutherford’s reproduction]; original letter uninspected. Chester County estate7520, [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=588&repo=r-24f48cc6 original will, pp588–589], previously inspected23October2026.</ref>


Samuel was born in 1761. He is the son of [[Glasgow-2870|John Glasgow]] and [[Cranmer-656|Mary Cranmer]].
== Research Notes ==
=== Candidate West Fallowfield estate ===

'''Original will, 23 October 2026:''' Samuel Glasgow of West Fallowfield names wife '''Tabitha''', infant daughter '''Margaret Ellen''', and a contingent remainder to the '''sons of his three brothers William, James and Robert Glasgow, of Ireland'''. The three named men are the testator’s brothers; the beneficiaries are their sons. This is not a clause naming the testator’s own son James. The will is dated '''17 May 1824'''; the proving endorsement is '''31 May 1824'''. [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=588&repo=r-24f48cc6 County original], file 7520, scanned volume 07451–7600, portal pp. 588–589 (downloaded extract pp. 3–4). Cover is portal p. 586. Original pages were visually read; the brother clause was independently reread.

The will appoints Robert Futhey and Thomas Stewart executors; estate office does not establish kinship. It also names Samuel Glasgow Haslett, described as James Haslett’s infant twin son; no godparent relationship is stated. His Glasgow middle name does not make him a Glasgow son. Later accounts, portal pp. 594 and 596, name Benjamin Glasgow as a debtor and William Glasgow in transmitting another estate’s legacy, without stating their relationship to the testator.

'''Profile identity:''' [[Glasgow-2872|Samuel Glasgow-2872]] remains a compatible candidate, not an established identification. His retained Cochranville locality and exact 17 May 1824 date fit this estate closely, but that date is the will date and may have been inherited as a death date. The will alone cannot prove death on that day. The profile’s Judith, who died in 1812, does not exclude a later Tabitha marriage. Its Pennsylvania birth/parent reconstruction and the brothers in Ireland need a combined family test rather than an automatic rejection or merge. No other local Tabitha or Margaret Ellen catalogue identity was found in the bounded duplicate check. The existing 72% father assessment and all family/vital fields are retained; this source does not name the testator’s father.

'''Missouri comparison:''' [[Glasgow-45|James Glasgow-45]], the probable Downington-born drummer, is not named in the inspected will or later accounts. That absence does not establish that he was not a son, but neither the military entry nor this estate selects a named father. The new Ireland relatives supply a concrete family to investigate while the immigrant-father/Philadelphia-estate tradition remains unproved. The complete downloaded estate extract is retained privately; no manuscript image is republished.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2870]] is assessed at 72% (probable). Samuel’s Chester/Nottingham generation and burial fit the maintained John/Mary Cranmer adult family and its Bible locator. Neither the memorial citation nor the unquoted Bible exposes a parent clause in the supplied dossier.

Named child to the specific adult family role represented by the selected father; independent earlier ancestry is outside this assessment.

Next useful test: Read the Glasgow Family Bible held at York Historic Trust and Samuel’s probate for an explicit father identification.
